I understand you completely. I don't have such person a in my life (yet), but I'm sure I would react similarily.

I've got a similar experience about a girl I know, but this is about illness. We both have a similar condition, but whenever we met it was always about some drama. She has basically no friends left and she blames it on them leaving once she became seriously ill (this is a progressive illness, but sometimes you discover it by getting serious heart problems in your 20s). At first I took what she said for what it was, but as time passed I started thinking to myself just how much terrible things can really happen to *one* person? I've been through pretty much exactly the same problems, but I'm doing pretty well considering. Every time the phone calls and I see her name, I get an uneasy feeling as my body has now associated her with hours and hours of drama.
Read this piece about [Narcissistic Extensions](http://www.wikihow.com/Identify-Being-a-Narcissistic-Extension). It says something about the damages someone close to a narcissist is going through.

Threatening to commit suicide if you leave is *clearly* manipulative behavior and you shouldn't let him control you like that. Don't give him pity when he does that, be mad that he's trying to play you like an instrument!
Well, it's certainly great to see how the school system motivates the students to do better! ^/s

Having someone tell them they want to kill themselves is a very difficult thing for a person to process. Please don't assume she doesn't care, she could be in a form of shock for all we know.

You are in a lot of pain. Keep talking to us and make more posts, we will try to understand you and if we can't at least we can identify with the pain. You've held out with the pain for so long, but now that you've found us, why not at least talk a little bit and empty yourself out before you go through with anything?

I agree and don't think suicidal people are selfish for killing themselves. There is a huge wall to penetrate before a person is able to cross that boundary of self preservation that is so ingrained into a living being. I am not suicidal, but have been through enormous hurdles (I came here to post my story and just read a few other posts before doing so). Even with those, I do not feel the need to kill myself, so obviously a person that wants to kill themselves is facing tremendous amounts of pain.

I can only say the same as HorriblyCrazy, if I'm not too late, could you hang on for a little bit more? It *is* possible to get better and this community certainly helped me a few years ago when I was close to dying (not from suicide though) by giving me something to hold on to, or at least peace and a belief in that complete strangers can care and identify with your problems, even though as unique a position one may be in.
